children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Delhi airport climbed 11 places to No 28 in OAG's ranking of the world's most connected international airports, the strongest showing by an Indian gateway in the 2026 report. IndiGo accounted for 40% of flights at the airport.

Delhi rose from No 39 in last year's ranking and was the only Indian airport to make the global top 50. It ranked ninth in the Asia-Pacific region and ninth among the world's low-cost megahubs. Delhi recorded 2,174 possible international connections in the ranking period, compared with 1,819 for Mumbai, as per OAG.

Mumbai, India's other major international gateway, ranked No 11 in the low-cost megahub category. IndiGo accounted for 43% of flights at Mumbai and 60% of the airport's low-cost-carrier capacity, compared with 57% at Delhi.

The two airports are the main international gateways in India, with Delhi handling a large share of the country's international connecting traffic and Mumbai serving as a major gateway between India and markets in the Middle East, Europe and Asia.

IndiGo's strong presence at both airports comes as the airline expands its international network alongside its dominant position in India's domestic market. The carrier has been adding overseas routes and capacity, including services to destinations across Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

title: Delhi Airport Rises to Top 30 in OAG's Global Megahub Ranking for 2026
